rv.q: For the rest of us the show is an unassailable treat and Eyre’s production has acquired the heart to go with its art.
This is an unbeatably splendid evening and quite the most delightful show to have entertained the capital in a long time.
The blockbuster revival of the 2004. Mary Poppins musical is a highly polished piece of entertainment, hugely uplifting and cheerful, with an undertow of melancholy and the occasional baggy moment.
Well, if money is no object, there are plenty of reasons to go for a family outing to see this version.
Half-baked story aside, ‘Mary Poppins’ serves up everything you could want in a mega-budget family musical: memorable songs, dazzling visuals and a nostalgic ideal of a London that never existed.
All contribute to a lavish if inescapably old-fashioned revival – sure to succeed commercially via the power of Poppins, but, unlike its titular nanny, never quite taking flight.

But for nearly three hours, at least, you can park some of those worries at the door, and simply bask in the gentle familiarity and delightful uplift of this story and the spit-spot production it has been given...
As grey clouds, wind and rain descend on London, Mary Poppins is back to lift us up with a burst of colour, magic and joy.
For all its strengths, Mary Poppins does not earn (or make the most of) this unusual length, especially given that it is, at its core, a family show.
Zizi Strallen in the title role has a clear and sublime singing voice, and her stage presence oozes charm and endearment.

All contribute to a lavish if somewhat muddled and inescapably old-fashioned revival – sure to succeed commercially via the nostalgic power of Poppins, but, unlike its titular nanny, never quite taking flight.
The magic of this production is that it allows us to set aside our boring sensible grown-up heads and not just remember but feel that time when we thought such things might be possible.
The Bank family home becomes a giant dollhouse, unfolding and sliding in and out like the pages of a pop-up book, bursting with colour and a childlike joy.
It is certainly hard to resist.
This magical performance of Mary Poppins will sweep you up with its charming cast, special effects and unbelievable set.
I highly recommend that you too should fly into the Prince Edward for a jolly old time!

cn.t: Critics find this polished, magical production a delightful family spectacle with dazzling effects and choreography, though some note it prioritizes technical efficiency over emotional depth.
